An overview of this role 
 As an Intermediate Backend Engineer (Python) in GitLab's Agent Foundations stage, you'll go beyond using AI tools. You'll help build the foundations for GitLab's agentic AI experiences: the platform that lets AI agents work across the whole software delivery lifecycle, not just write code. That covers the reusable building blocks agents and flows are made from as well as our core harness, Duo Developer.
 Most of your work will be backend engineering in Python, using libraries such as LangGraph to build secure, reliable and scalable features in our AI Gateway. You'll also work across the stack where needed. You'll work closely with engineers across the stage and other AI Engineering teams. This is a high-visibility area where GitLab's core platform meets its AI strategy.
 What you'll do 
 Develop, ship and maintain features for the Duo Agent Platform in the Duo Workflow Service, the AI Gateway and, where needed, the GitLab monolith. Keep them secure, well-tested and performant.
 Build and improve agentic flows and their reusable parts with LangChain and LangGraph, including the Flow Registry.
 Work with Product Management, UX, frontend, backend and AI specialists to refine requirements and ship improvements in small iterations.
 Design, implement and review APIs (including GraphQL and REST) and the backend logic behind them, with reliable, scalable and clear contracts for clients such as the GitLab monolith, IDE extensions and Duo CLI.
 Improve and extend automated testing (pytest and other frameworks), including evaluations of agent and flow behavior, to strengthen quality and give developers faster feedback.
 Share standards, patterns and learnings with other engineers to raise the bar for responsible AI integration and evidence-driven engineering.
 Join Tier 2 on-call rotations to troubleshoot production issues, contribute to root cause analysis, and improve observability and resiliency.
 Keep an eye on the competitive landscape to help keep GitLab's agent platform best-in-class as more work becomes agentic.
 Take part in on-call or operational support where your team’s ownership model requires it.
 What you'll bring 
 Experience building and maintaining production Python backend applications, including APIs, asynchronous or background processing, and data models.
 Experience with LLM application frameworks such as LangGraph, or designing and shipping AI-powered backend features or harnesses.
 Skill in designing or extending APIs (REST, GraphQL or gRPC) with attention to scalability, maintainability and backward compatibility.
 Comfort working across the stack in a mature codebase. Familiarity with Ruby on Rails and/or JavaScript and Vue is a plus.
 Experience finding and fixing performance bottlenecks in applications.
 Clear written and verbal communication, including technical proposals and documentation, in a remote, async, cross-functional team.
 Openness to learning and to applying skills from related technologies or fields.
 About the team 
 The Agent Foundations stage builds the foundations for GitLab's agentic AI experiences. We provide the platform, catalog and execution features that help teams deliver resilient agents and flows to customers. The stage has three groups: Agent Developer, AI Catalog and Agent Execution. Between them, they own the GitLab Duo Developer foundational flow and the Flow Registry; the AI Catalog, including custom agents, custom flows and external agent integrations; and agent execution, agent tools and agent observability.
 Our engineers work async-first across EMEA, AMER, and India timezones. We work with teams across AI engineering and the rest of GitLab so the Duo Agent Platform can power many of GitLab's AI features.

 What we value 
 Accuracy, and the habit of checking your own work before anyone else has to.
 Finishing what you own without being chased.
 Understanding how each entity earns and spends money.
 Discretion with confidential financial information.
 Curiosity, and a willingness to fix a process that keeps producing the same error.
 The honesty to say when something is wrong, including your own work.
 What you'll do 
 Keep payables accurate and vendors paid on time

 Apply cash receipts, maintain the AR aging, and handle first-level collection follow-up, flagging past-due accounts and disputes to the Controller for escalation.
 Support the month-end close

 Prepare standard and recurring journal entries with full supporting documentation for Controller review and approval, then upload the approved files to NetSuite and verify posting accuracy.
 Run intercompany confirmations: prepare balance confirmations, circulate them to group entities, follow up, and assemble settlement support.
 Keep records audit-ready and support the Controller
 File and archive supporting documentation per the established folder structure, pull samples and documents requested by external auditors, and keep audit folders current.
 Handle finance requests in Jira, gathering documentation, keeping tickets updated and closing them once resolved. Write and maintain the procedures for the tasks you own.
 Work with the Controller on ad hoc requests and special projects: onboarding new entities or acquisitions, opening and closing bank accounts, system implementations, and data gathering for analyses and reporting.  Two to four years of full-cycle accounting experience.

 Self-direction and organisation. You can carry a high volume of recurring tasks with minimal supervision.
 Follow-through. You chase the missing approval, receipt, or confirmation until it arrives.
 Discretion and judgement with confidential financial information.
 Clear writing. You can explain a reconciling item or a vendor discrepancy in a few lines.

 Useful experience 
 Multi-entity or multi-currency accounting.
 Power Query.
 Payments, fintech, or software.
 Using a corporate banking portal.
 Jira.
 Writing procedures for a finance team that is still being built.
 Who will enjoy this role 
 You notice when a vendor statement doesn't match, a bank line has no home, or an intercompany balance is off by the same amount two months running. You want to know why, and you fix the cause.
 In one week you might clear an invoice batch across three entities, chase a cardholder for receipts, reconcile an AUD bank account, and pull audit samples. Most of the work recurs, and the value is in getting it right every time.
 The hard parts are specific. Volume is high and the close date doesn't move. Across seven currencies and several entities, small mistakes compound. You prepare and the Controller decides: accounting judgement and final approvals sit with someone else. Processes are being built as the team grows, so sometimes you'll do a task that has no procedure yet, then write one.

 Group Ventures builds companies for Valsoft, and its growth has been recognized on Deloitte's Technology Fast 50. You'll see how a multi-entity, multi-currency technology group runs from the inside, and as the team scales there is room to take on more analytical work.

BUILD SOMETHING PEOPLE LOVE

Wealthsimple is Canada’s leading financial innovator. The company offers a full suite of simple, sophisticated financial products across managed investing, do-it-yourself trading, cryptocurrency, tax filing, spending and saving. Wealthsimple currently serves more than 4 million Canadians and holds over $169 billion in assets under administration. The company was founded in 2014 by a team of financial experts and technology entrepreneurs, and is headquartered in Toronto, Canada.

About the team

Over 30,000 Canadian businesses already trust Wealthsimple Business to spend, invest, and help their employees save, all in one place. But most Canadian SMBs still don't know we offer business banking at all. Our team owns the growth engine that closes that gap: getting Wealthsimple Business in front of the millions of small businesses in Canada who haven't heard of it yet, and building the pipeline that lets us compete directly for a market that isn't ours yet. We work closely with the broader Marketing org but stay focused on this segment specifically. This isn't general brand awareness — it's demand for a product category most SMBs haven't considered us for.

 
 

ABOUT THE ROLE

You'll own net-new customer acquisition for the SMB segment: running the paid and experimental channels that create demand where none currently exists. This is a build-from-scratch role in a real sense. The acquisition engine for this segment doesn't exist yet, so you'll be defining it, testing what moves the needle, and scaling what works, rather than optimizing something already in motion.

 
 

WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own SMB-specific acquisition: explore and test across channel types, paid media, partnerships, content, community, and anything else that could move the needle. No one's handing you a channel mix. Figuring that out is the job

 - Run the team's growth experimentation cadence: CAC/LTV analysis and funnel experiments that turn into repeatable, scalable campaigns, not one-off tests, measured through to pipeline handed to Sales

 - Test positioning and messaging that gets this segment to notice us for the first time

 - Own growth-motivated webinars and other programs aimed at reaching new audiences, not nurturing ones we already have

 - Partner with the Demand Gen Specialist so acquisition experiments feed nurture, and nurture insights inform where acquisition effort goes next

 - Embed AI into your day-to-day, creative and copy iteration, audience research, campaign experimentation, to move faster and test more

 
 

WHAT YOU BRING

 - 4–6+ years in growth or performance marketing, with a track record of generating demand and measuring it through to downstream pipeline value

 - Experience building and running growth experiments: channel tests, funnel optimization, CAC/LTV analysis. You don't just execute a media plan someone else designed

 - Comfort operating in a segment or product with limited brand awareness. You understand how messaging, channel mix, and creative have to work differently when you're introducing a category to someone who doesn't know it exists yet, not comparing features for someone who already does

 We've grown fast, and we're investing in the systems behind that money flow to match. We're hiring a Senior Product Manager to own it end to end: from rate card to invoice to cash, and from carrier bill to audited cost.
 About Portless
 Portless is changing the face of global e-commerce. By decoupling brands from traditional, expensive domestic warehousing, we let e-commerce companies ship directly from manufacturing hubs to global consumers in as little as three to five days.
 We move packages to 75+ countries for hundreds of DTC brands, with millions of packages shipped annually, 99.8% pick-and-pack accuracy, and 98% on-time delivery. We're a small, remote-first team growing fast, and the work you do here shows up in a merchant's business, and on our own books, within weeks.

 Cost audit (procure to pay). Ingesting carrier and partner invoices, matching them to what we shipped, and catching discrepancies automatically.
 Margin visibility. A shipment-level view of revenue, cost and pass-through charges that finance and leadership can rely on.
 Duties and taxes. How tariffs, VAT and other pass-through charges are calculated, billed and collected, in close partnership with our compliance team.

 An end-to-end view of how money moves through Portless today, and a clear picture of where it needs to go

 Our largest carriers' invoices matched and audited automatically

 Measurable time given back to the finance and CS teams

 Product craft first. This is the bar we're least flexible on.

Reports to: CEO 
 Location: Hybrid – North America (HQ: Vancouver, BC) 
 About CO280 
 CO280 is a leading developer of low-carbon industrial infrastructure projects. As a top 3 global BECCS developer, we hold more than $1B in signed CDR offtakes from buyers including Microsoft, Google, JPMorgan, Salesforce, and Stripe. We pioneered BECCS in North America, partnering with the continent's largest pulp and paper companies to retrofit mills with carbon capture and sequestration and deliver permanent carbon removal at scale. 
 We are now expanding to deliver low-carbon power solutions across the data center market, applying key advantages we already possess: trusted hyperscaler relationships, a portfolio of pre-qualified industrial sites, expertise in energy and CCS project development and access to capital. We've identified and pre-qualified more than 20 industrial sites representing approximately 6 GW of potential capacity — not just parcels of land, but strategic infrastructure platforms with existing industrial zoning, water rights, transmission access, and established host relationships that dramatically compress development timelines in a market where speed-to-power is everything. 
 This is the rare moment when a market this large is gated by a problem this specific. The AI buildout is the defining industrial expansion of the decade, and power is the constraint holding it back, with interconnection queues running four to seven years and the industry defaulting to unabated gas it does not want to burn. CO280 is building the platform that answers it.  
 You'll join a close-knit team of entrepreneurial, collaborative, and transparent operators who have developed, delivered, and scaled new technologies and industrial infrastructure across multiple verticals.  We believe clean power must be practical, bankable, and scalable to move the needle on net zero and earn social license. If you want to help build the projects the energy transition is waiting on, this is a seat at the table. 
 The Role 
 The Vice President Project Development will build and lead CO280's low carbon power data center infrastructure platform — owning project origination, development strategy, strategic partnerships, and the project development organization. You will identify, originate, secure, and advance gigawatt-scale infrastructure opportunities from concept through Final Investment Decision (FID), working across utilities, industrial hosts, OEMs, EPCs, hyperscalers, AI developers, and capital partners to turn strategic sites into bankable projects. 
 This is a relationship-driven leadership role. Success will depend as much on the executive relationships you bring as the projects you've delivered. Existing relationships across hyperscalers, neoclouds, data center developers, utilities, power developers, OEMs, EPCs, infrastructure investors, and other strategic partners will enable CO280 to originate opportunities faster and build projects that competitors cannot. 
 Solutions may span gas-to-power + CCS, biomass, and solar with storage — owned and operated by CO280 and/or with partners. You own development through FID; at FID, the project engineering team leads execution, with your continued commercial support through construction to commercial operation. 
 This role exists because the AI industry has discovered that compute is no longer constrained by chips — it's constrained by power. Every major hyperscaler is competing to secure gigawatts of generation capacity while utilities face interconnection queues measured in years. CO280 is uniquely positioned to solve that problem by combining strategic industrial sites, deep customer relationships, and proven infrastructure development expertise. The Vice President Project Development will convert those advantages into one of North America's largest low-carbon infrastructure portfolios. 
 Your first 12–18 months will include: 
 Building CO280's project development function and playbook. 
 Converting pre-qualified host sites into data center-ready opportunities. 
 Securing the company's first anchor AI infrastructure customers. 
 Advancing the first one or two projects to Final Investment Decision. 
 Key Responsibilities 
 Origination & Development 
 Drive new low-carbon power projects from origination through FID, then support the project engineering team commercially through construction to commercial operation. 
 Develop CO280's project origination strategy by matching industrial host sites with hyperscaler demand, transmission availability, fiber infrastructure and regional power market opportunities. 
 Own the development budget and project economics for each project through stage-gates to FID, including scenario and sensitivity analysis on key inputs. 
 Partnerships & Commercial 
 Build executive relationships with utilities, industrial hosts, hyperscalers, neoclouds, data center developers, OEMs, EPCs, gas suppliers, and strategic partners across the project value chain. 
 Negotiate contracts with project partners, working closely with project engineering, finance, legal, community engagement, and commercial teams. 
 Partner with the commercial team to map the hyperscaler and AI-buyer channel end-to-end, translating buyer needs directly into project design and the development roadmap. 
 Cross-Functional Delivery 
 Partner with engineering to develop technically robust, commercially attractive, and financeable projects, including coordinating studies, and building relationships with OEM and EPC partners. 
 Align with finance to ensure projects are bankable, supporting project economic models and corporate/project financing activities. 
 Manage the operating cadence — stage-gates, risk registers, development-budget discipline, and project economic performance. 
 Leadership & Strategy 
 Build and lead the project development team: hiring, operating cadence, stage-gate process, and development budgets. 
 Shape CO280's long-term infrastructure strategy as a member of the executive leadership team, defining where the business plays, how it wins, and how it scales. 
 Serve on the executive leadership team and represent CO280 externally with customers, partners, investors, and industry stakeholders. 
 This is an opportunity to build one of North America's leading AI infrastructure development platforms at the point where energy, industrial redevelopment and hyperscale computing converge. 
 Location 
 Preference for Houston, Dallas, Denver or Vancouver but these locations are not a requirement. 
 At least 30% travel across North America 
 Qualifications 
 We're looking for a leader who combines: 
 A proven track record developing large-scale energy infrastructure projects through final Investment Decision. 
 The entrepreneurial mindset to build a new business in a rapidly evolving market. 
 The commercial, financial and relationship-building capability to originate, structure and finance bankable infrastructure projects. 
 Required 
 15+ years of relevant project development experience in power, energy infrastructure, or digital infrastructure, with a track record of taking projects from origination to FID and, ideally, to COD. 
 An established executive network across utilities, Independent Power Producers, OEMs, EPCs, infrastructure developers, investors, or hyperscaler infrastructure teams. 
 Demonstrated success originating and commercializing new infrastructure opportunities with sophisticated corporate customers and partners. 
 Deep experience developing utility-scale power infrastructure: generation, transmission, interconnection, permitting, and site development. Experience supporting hyperscale data centers is highly desirable but not essential. 
 Strong commercial, financial and engineering fluency, with the ability to structure bankable infrastructure projects and communicate effectively with technical, commercial and investment stakeholders. 
 Demonstrated ability to contribute to term sheets and definitive agreements with sophisticated counterparties — hyperscalers, AI-native buyers, industrial hosts, midstream operators, or strategic investors. 
 Experience building and running a development team, with clear views on stage-gates, risk allocation, and development budgets.

Vous êtes chef de cuisine et vous rêvez de travailler au Québec ? 
 Vous cherchez une cuisine où vous avez enfin la main sur la carte, une petite équipe, et un cadre qui donne envie de se lever le matin. Ça tombe bien. 
 À propos de l'employeur 
 S'installer au Canada, ce n'est pas juste changer de pays. C'est aussi choisir un endroit où on a envie de travailler tous les jours.
 Ici, c'est une auberge-restaurant installée dans une maison ancestrale, sur la Côte-de-Beaupré, face au fleuve Saint-Laurent. Vingt minutes de Québec, dix minutes du Mont-Sainte-Anne. Huit chambres rénovées à l'étage, un restaurant au rez-de-chaussée, et une réputation solide auprès des gens du coin comme des touristes qui viennent de France, des États-Unis et de partout au Canada.
 On y sert entre 35 et 50 couverts sur un service classique, et plus de 100 quand il y a un mariage ou un événement. L'été, ça tourne fort. Le reste de l'année, la clientèle locale prend le relais, avec le brunch du dimanche qui est une institution.
 L'entreprise compte 23 personnes, dont une brigade de cuisine de 5 au maximum. Autant dire qu'on se connaît tous, et que le patron est joignable directement.
 Votre rôle 
 Vous prenez la direction de la cuisine. La production quotidienne, l'équipe, les commandes, et surtout la carte.
 Le menu québécois traditionnel reste : c'est ce que les touristes viennent chercher, et il fait partie de l'identité de la maison. À côté, vous avez la main libre pour développer une carte plus contemporaine, avec vos influences — cuisine québécoise moderne, italienne, française. C'est exactement ce que la clientèle locale attend.
 Vos missions 
 ● Superviser une équipe de 4 à 5 personnes (2 assistants et des plongeurs) et gérer les horaires.
 ● Assurer la production : mise en place en journée, présence au piano le soir.
 ● Gérer les commandes et les approvisionnements.
 ● Faire vivre la carte : proposer, tester, renouveler les plats.
 ● Animer une réunion hebdomadaire avec l'équipe.
 ● Travailler main dans la main avec la salle — ici, la cohésion cuisine-service fait toute la différence.
 ● Gérer le brunch du dimanche et les services événementiels (mariages, groupes).
 Profil recherché 
 ● Vous avez déjà tenu un poste de chef, ou vous êtes un second prêt à passer le cap.
 ● Vous savez faire tourner une petite brigade sans usine à gaz.
 ● Vous êtes autonome sur les commandes et la gestion de production.
 ● Vous avez des idées et l'envie de les mettre à la carte.
 ● Vous respectez une cuisine du terroir avant de vouloir la réinventer — ici, la tradition québécoise se travaille, elle ne s'efface pas.
 ● Vous voulez vous installer durablement au Québec.
 Conditions proposées 
 ● Poste permanent à temps plein.
 ● Salaire de 30 $ à 35 $ de l'heure , et jusqu'à 36 $ et plus selon votre expérience et vos compétences.
 ● Logement temporaire offert sur place à votre arrivée, dans les chambres de l'auberge — vous avez le temps de vous poser avant de chercher.
 ● Une vraie liberté sur la carte contemporaine.
 ● Une petite équipe et un lien direct avec la direction : pas de couches de management, les décisions se prennent vite.
 ● Un cadre de travail entre le fleuve et la montagne, à 20 minutes de Québec.
 Expatriation & accompagnement 
 Selon votre profil et votre situation, ce recrutement peut passer par le programme Jeunes Professionnels (EIC) ou par un permis de travail avec EIMT . Nos équipes évaluent avec vous la meilleure voie dès le premier échange.

 ● accompagnement dans votre installation au Québec.

 BDO GrantMatch is a leading government funding consultancy with more than 20 years of experience helping organizations across Canada and the United States identify, secure, and manage government funding. 
 Our team works with organizations across virtually every industry – from advanced manufacturing, food processing and clean technology to aerospace, municipalities and other public-sector organizations – supporting projects involving capital investment, innovation, workforce development, sustainability, 
 infrastructure and economic growth. 
 Our experience and extensive funding knowledge also power GrantMatch™, our proprietary technology platform used to identify and evaluate government funding opportunities across North America. 
 As our team continues to grow, we are seeking three Funding Analysts to join BDO GrantMatch remotely from anywhere in Canada. One position will require professional fluency in both English and French. 
 The Opportunity 
 If you are an exceptional researcher and writer who enjoys learning about new industries, solving problems and turning complex information into a compelling business case, this role may be an excellent fit. The Funding Analyst is a critical member of our client delivery team and is responsible for 
 researching and developing the written content required for government funding applications. 
 Approximately 70% of the role is focused on research and professional business writing. You will regularly move between industries, clients, and subject areas. On one project, you may be researching automated food-processing equipment; on another, clean technology, aerospace manufacturing, municipal infrastructure or an innovative production process. 
 You will work closely with our Funding Specialists, who lead client relationships, project scoping, information gathering, and overall funding strategy. Together, the Funding Specialist and Funding Analyst transform a client's project concept into a comprehensive, accurate, and compelling funding application. 
 What You'll Do 
 Research & Grant Application Development 
 Research clients, industries, technologies, equipment, production processes, markets and other technical or business topics required to develop strong funding applications. 
 Become a project-level subject matter expert, developing enough knowledge of unfamiliar industries and technologies to communicate complex concepts clearly and credibly. 
 Draft comprehensive government funding applications, business cases, proposals and supporting documentation on behalf of clients. 
 Translate technical, financial, and operational information into clear, persuasive narratives aligned with government funding priorities. 
 Review program guidelines, application forms, and supporting documentation to develop a thorough understanding of eligibility requirements, evaluation criteria, program objectives and submission requirements. 
 Identify key program language and ensure applications clearly demonstrate alignment between the client's proposed project and the funder's objectives. 
 Develop application templates, checklists, and other working documents to ensure all required information and supporting documentation are addressed. 
 Adhere to our in-house Style Guide and standards for written content. Conduct detailed selfreviews of your work for accuracy, completeness, consistency, grammar, and overall quality before applications move through the broader review process. 
 Incorporate feedback from Funding Specialists, internal reviewers, and clients while maintaining consistency across the complete application package. 
 Project Strategy & Collaboration 
 Partner closely with Funding Specialists to understand each client's business, proposed project, and overall funding strategy. 
 Participate in relevant client meetings to gain first-hand knowledge of projects, ask questions and capture the information required for application development. 
 Build on the Funding Specialist's initial project strategy to develop a comprehensive and compelling application narrative. 
 Identify information gaps throughout the writing process and develop thoughtful, customized questions that enable Funding Specialists to efficiently gather the required information from clients. 
 Maintain proactive communication with Funding Specialists regarding application progress, outstanding information, upcoming deadlines, and potential risks. 
 Collaborate with colleagues across the BDO GrantMatch team to share program knowledge, research, and best practices. 
 Government Funding Research 
 Research new and existing government funding programs across Canada and the United States. 
 Interpret complex program guidelines and translate them into practical eligibility requirements, funding considerations, and application strategies. 
 Identify programs that may align with existing client projects and communicate potential opportunities to the broader team. 
 Stay informed about government priorities, economic developments, emerging industries and business trends that may influence funding opportunities. 
 Contribute research and program intelligence to BDO GrantMatch's internal funding knowledge base and proprietary technology platform. 
 Project Management & Quality 
 Manage multiple applications and research assignments simultaneously, often with competing priorities and firm external deadlines. 
 Develop and maintain realistic workback schedules in collaboration with Funding Specialists. 
 Take ownership of assigned deliverables and ensure work is completed accurately and on time, with sufficient time for internal and client review. 
 Maintain organized electronic project files and documentation using Microsoft 365 and SharePoint. 
 Track application progress and communicate status, information requirements, and potential challenges proactively. 
 Support application submission and post-approval/compliance activities where required. 
 Participate in team initiatives, knowledge sharing, and special projects that improve the quality and efficiency of BDO GrantMatch's services. 
 What We're Looking For 
 Above all, we are looking for an exceptional writer and researcher with strong business judgment. The successful candidate will demonstrate: 
 Exceptional professional writing skills. You can take large volumes of complex or technical information and turn them into clear, concise and persuasive written content. 
 Strong research skills and intellectual curiosity. You enjoy learning how businesses, technologies, and industries work and are comfortable becoming knowledgeable about unfamiliar subjects quickly. 
 Analytical thinking. You can interpret detailed program criteria, identify what matters most, and connect a client's project to broader government objectives. 
 Strong business sense. You understand how to identify the most compelling elements of a business or project and communicate its economic, operational, and strategic value. 
 Exceptional attention to detail. You recognize that application quality can depend on everything from a strong project narrative to an overlooked eligibility requirement or inconsistent figure. 
 Ownership and accountability. You take responsibility for the quality, accuracy, and timeliness of your work and proactively identify information gaps, risks, and next steps. 
 Excellent organization and time management. You can manage multiple assignments and deadlines without losing sight of details. 
 Strong collaboration skills. You are comfortable working closely with Funding Specialists, clients, and other team members in a highly integrated virtual environment. 
 Initiative and self-motivation. You are comfortable working independently, asking thoughtful questions, and seeking out the information you need to move work forward. 
 Adaptability. You enjoy variety and can comfortably move between different clients, industries, funding programs, and project types. 
 A commitment to continuous learning and quality. You actively seek feedback and look for opportunities to strengthen both your own work and our team's approach. 
 Education & Experience

ABOUT THE ROLE

The Enterprise Trust & Governance team builds the control plane that lets the world’s largest organizations deploy Perplexity broadly and with confidence. Computer and our agents work across a growing share of our customers’ environments, tools, and models. For administrators, that makes precise, enforceable control essential: who can do what, with which data, through which agents, and within what usage limits. This team makes those controls easy to manage, reliable and consistent across every product, and transparent to the people accountable for them.

This is a product and platform engineering role with end-to-end ownership, from shaping the architecture and policy models to shipping the experiences our customers’ administrators and security teams use every day. You’ll work across product and infrastructure teams to turn complex enterprise requirements into reusable primitives and intuitive controls. The scope spans identity and provisioning, fine-grained role-based access across connectors, tool actions, and models, customer-managed encryption keys, admin APIs, audit logs, and policy and usage controls. Strong governance helps enterprises move from pilots to company-wide rollouts and gives them the confidence to entrust agents with greater responsibility over time.




KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Own enterprise identity and provisioning, including SSO (SAML/OIDC), SCIM, WorkOS integrations, and support for identity providers such as Okta and Microsoft Entra ID.

 - Build the permissions platform, with fine-grained roles and permissions for connectors, tool actions, models, and model effort levels, enforced consistently across products and agent workflows.

 - Design and ship secure, well-documented admin APIs for audit logs, members, groups, roles, and settings.

 - Build policy controls for model and feature availability, staged rollouts, model deprecations, usage and spend limits, alerts, and cost-center allocation.

 - Build admin-facing analytics for adoption, usage, spend, and policy enforcement, helping organizations measure value and manage their deployments.

 - Deliver audit logs and change notifications that help administrators investigate activity, track configuration changes, and support compliance.

 - Set the technical bar for authorization correctness and reliability, with fast, consistent, explainable permission checks, well-defined failure behavior, and strong tenant isolation.

 - Partner with Product, Design, Security, Sales, and Customer Success to translate complex enterprise requirements into reusable platform capabilities and intuitive admin experiences.
   
   


QUALIFICATIONS

 - 4+ years of software engineering experience, with a track record of owning complex backend systems from design through production operation.

 - Strong system design skills, including building reliable, scalable, multi-tenant SaaS platforms with clear security and isolation boundaries.

 - Strong proficiency in a backend language such as Python, Go, or Rust, and hands-on experience with cloud infrastructure such as AWS and Kubernetes.

 - Deep expertise in at least one of the following:
   
   - Enterprise identity and provisioning, including OAuth, OIDC, SAML, and SCIM.
   
   - Permissions platforms, fine-grained authorization, and policy enforcement.
   
   - Encryption, customer-managed keys, and key lifecycle management.
   
   - Enterprise admin platforms, audit infrastructure, or usage and spend analytics.

 - Experience building or integrating enterprise identity and access systems, including platforms such as WorkOS, Okta, or Microsoft Entra ID.

 Own revenue recognition and every judgmental or complex accounting entry across all entities, including usage-based and payfac revenue under IFRS

 Set technical accounting policy for the group, and make sure it's applied consistently across entities in different jurisdictions

 WHAT YOU'LL BRING 
 CPA designation (or equivalent international designation)
 5+ years of progressive accounting experience, including ownership of technical accounting

 On-Target Earnings (OTE): For a high performer after ramp: $384,000/year at 20 deals/month. Stretch for elite top tier performance: $576,000/year at 25 deals/month. No cap.
 Average Deal Size: $16,000, with higher-tier packages at $30,000+
 Leads: Mostly inbound prospects from cold traffic, plus a smaller amount from organic content, pre-qualified by application form and setters.
 We’re looking for the best closers in the game. You get a full calendar of high-ticket calls, a $16,000 average deal, and 10% on every dollar you collect, rising to 12% when you hit the stretch bonus.
 About Limitless Agency 
 Limitless Agency helps digital marketing agency owners build businesses that scale and sell. Our core program, Limitless Black Card, combines one-on-one strategy with the founders, implementation support, weekly group coaching, a dedicated account team, and in-person sessions at our Tampa headquarters. We’ve worked with hundreds of agency owners and helped many reach six-figure monthly revenue.
 We spend well over six figures a month on paid acquisition. We have an in-depth application form and setters qualifying the leads. Our sales team closes 25 to 50 high-ticket deals a month and we're in the process of scaling. Your job is to turn a full calendar into cash.
 Website: https://limitlessagency.io/ 
 The Opportunity 
 Every deal you close pays $1,600 at our average deal size when paid in full, and up to $3,000 on a top package in a stretch month. For paid in full deals, hit 20 deals and you’re at $32,000 for the month, 25 and your rate jumps to 12% on the whole month to $48,000. For payment plans you're paid as cash is collected.
 The Role 
 This is a pure inbound closing seat. We can fill your calendar as long as you can perform. You’ll take back-to-back calls with agency owners who found us through paid ads, and you’ll close them.
 These are inbound prospects coming from cold traffic. Most had never heard of us before they saw an ad. They aren’t referrals, and they haven’t sat through a webinar that warmed them up. You build trust, find the real problem, and close a $16,000+ decision on the call. If you’ve done this with cold paid traffic, this is one of the best seats you’ll find.
 What You’ll Do 
 Run back-to-back high-ticket sales calls with cold prospects from paid ads, booked by our setters.
 Close a minimum of 15 deals a month, with a stretch goal of 25.
 Run our sales process with precision on every call and own the outcome.
 Follow up relentlessly on pipeline, no-shows, and open decisions to recover and close deals.
 Work closely with the setters to keep the calendar full of qualified prospects.
 Keep clean notes and pipeline stages in GoHighLevel so nothing slips.
 Review your own calls, take coaching, and keep sharpening your numbers.
 How Compensation Works 
 This is straight commission on cash collected, with no base and no cap. Some clients pay in full and some are on payment plans, so you get paid as the money comes in. Close 25 deals in a month and your rate goes from 10% to 12% on all cash collected from that month’s deals, not just the deals above 25.
 Commission per deal:
 $15,000 deal: $1,500 at 10% / $1,800 at 12% (stretch month)
 $16,000 deal (average): $1,600 at 10% / $1,920 at 12% (stretch month)
 $25,000 deal (higher package): $2,500 at 10% / $3,000 at 12% (stretch month)
 Earning Potential 
 Here’s what a month looks like at different levels, using our $16,000 average deal. Bigger packages pay more. These are examples, not guarantees.
 Ramp (first 1–2 months): 10 deals at 10% = $16,000/month ($192,000 annualized)
 Minimum standard: 15 deals at 10% = $24,000/month ($288,000 annualized)
 On target: 20 deals at 10% = $32,000/month ($384,000 annualized)
 Stretch goal (12% unlocked): 25 deals at 12% = $48,000/month ($576,000 annualized)
 Math at target: 20 deals × $16,000 × 10% = $32,000 a month. At stretch: 25 deals × $16,000 × 12% = $48,000 a month.
 The Kicker: At 24 deals, you’ve earned $38,400. Close one more and the whole month reprices to 12%: $48,000. That’s a $9,600 raise for one deal, every month you get there.
 Who Thrives Here 
 This seat is built for a closer at the top of their game. You’re competitive, you own your numbers, and you’d rather have uncapped commission than a base. You can walk into a call with a stranger from a Facebook ad and walk out with a $16,000 decision. You follow up without being told, and you take coaching without getting defensive.
 If you need a base to lean on, or you’ve only closed warm buyers, this isn’t the seat for you.
 Non-Negotiable Requirements 
 We’re hiring the top closers in the market. Every finalist must meet all of these and be able to prove it.
 2+ years of successful high-ticket closing experience, ideally with some B2B and/or agency background
 A proven track record closing $15,000+ deals and $150k+ months, with documentation to prove it.
 Experience closing inbound cold prospects from cold traffic. Not just warm referrals, and not just webinar or event closes.
 Availability for a full-time, full calendar, full commitment.
 Exclusivity 
 This seat comes with a full calendar, and we expect your full attention. You can’t be on other offers, take sales calls for anyone else, or run a side business or side hustle. If you’re closing for someone else on the side, this isn’t the role for you.
 Prove It

 Commission statements, payout reports, or pay stubs showing what you earned.
 CRM or dashboard screenshots showing deals closed, deal sizes, and close rate.
 Recorded sales calls where you closed a $15,000+ deal with a cold prospect.
 References from sales managers or business owners you’ve closed for.
 If you can’t show it, we can’t consider you.
 Uncapped commission: 10% of cash collected on every deal, with no ceiling on earnings.
